book.title: Alfred C. Kinsey: A Public-Private Life

evidence: trade publisher signal: W. W. Norton / W. W. Norton & Company

argument.statement: Jones shows that Alfred C. Kinsey’s public image as a disinterested biologist was a carefully crafted persona, masking his work as a social reformer focused on destroying sexual repression.

book.rationale: The book is a biography of Alfred C. Kinsey, focusing on his life and contributions to the field of human sexuality, while also addressing broader societal impacts, thus justifying the additional subjects.
book.summary: In this brilliant biography of sex researcher Alfred C. Kinsey, Jones unlocks the long-closed archives of the Kinsey Institute to present a moving & even shocking portrait of the man who pierced the veil of reticence surrounding human sexuality. Here is an incisive portrait that truly separates the myth from the man. Shows that the public image of disinterested biologist cultivated by Kinsey was a carefully crafted public persona. The Kinsey who emerges here was a social reformer who devoted his every waking hour to the destruction of sexual repression. Kinsey's life is much more than the story of a scientist who sparked the cultural debate of our century. His odyssey illustrates in microcosm the transition from Victorian to modern times. Photos.
